hints: Look carefully at the top right of the graph. Does line Q eventually reach the same maximum rate as line P, just more slowly?
Recall which type of inhibition can be overcome by adding lots more substrate, and which type lowers the maximum rate no matter how much substrate you add.
walkthrough:
**Read what the graph is telling us**

Look at line P and line Q. At low substrate concentration, Q is slower than P. But at very high substrate concentration, Q catches up and reaches the same maximum rate of reaction.

So the key clue is: same Vmax, but lower rate at first.

**Link the shape to competitive inhibition**

A competitive inhibitor competes with substrate for the active site. At low substrate, it slows the rate. At very high substrate, there is so much substrate that it outcompetes the inhibitor, so Vmax is still reached.

A non-competitive inhibitor attaches elsewhere, changes enzyme shape, and lowers Vmax permanently. Extra substrate cannot overcome it.

**Check statements 1 to 4**

Statement 1 describes non-competitive inhibition. This would lower the maximum rate, so it cannot give line Q.

Statements 2 and 3 both describe competitive inhibition. Similar shape to substrate means it fits the active site. Blocking the active site also means competition. Both can be overcome by high substrate, so both fit line Q.

Statement 4 starts at optimum temperature. Going higher will denature some enzyme and lower Vmax permanently, so it cannot give line Q.

**Pick the correct combination**

Only 2 and 3 fit the graph. That is option D, 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Includes 1 and 4 which both lower Vmax. Line Q shows the same Vmax as P, so this combination is wrong.
options.B: Both 1 (non-competitive) and 4 (denaturation above optimum) would prevent the reaction reaching the original maximum rate, unlike line Q.
options.C: Although 2 and 3 are correct, adding 4 (higher than optimum temperature) would lower Vmax, so Q would not catch up to P.
options.D: Both 2 and 3 describe competitive inhibition at the active site, which slows the rate at first but still allows the same Vmax at high substrate, exactly matching line Q.
